note: Expected findings are the code, path, message and suggestion `orb validate` (the Rust validator) reports for the same program. Added cases copy page.rs test_page_missing_name and follow validate_page's PascalCase branch (check_naming is the English-program flag, as for the path character check). The real-program-shape cases feed a lowered std atom to the rule: the rule must reach LINT_FINISH (a runtime type error in the findings expression leaves the transition without it). The program, the raw text and the decided language arrive as LINT_INPUT from std-orb-lint-input; a page with a protocol (boot, http, stdio) carries an address, not a path, so only route pages are held to the path checks.

program.name: std-reminder-scheduler
program.description: std-reminder-scheduler — deadline reminders for a target entity. A periodic tick scans the target for records whose `dateField` deadline (a ms-epoch number or an ISO datetime string) is within `offsetHours` of now and that have not been reminded yet, and emits `ReminderDue` for each — every matching record, via a self-driving scan loop. `direction` picks which side of now the scan matches: 'future' (default) fires for deadlines up to `offsetHours` ahead; 'past' fires once a record's date is at least `offsetHours` behind now. Marks each record `remindedAt` so it isn't reminded twice — and only when the record actually matched the scan, so records outside the window stay eligible for later passes. Compose alongside std-notify-on-event to deliver the reminder.

fields.description: The entity to which the reminder applies.

fields.description: The number of records processed during this run.

fields.description: Deadline timestamp (also lets the standalone default target validate).

fields.description: Scratch: id of the record the scan loop is currently reminding.

offsetHours.label: How many hours before the deadline to remind?
offsetHours.description: A reminder fires once the deadline is within this many hours of now.
offsetHours.synonyms: advance notice, lead time, heads up, early warning hours, how far ahead

enabled.label: Send deadline reminders
enabled.description: Automatically remind about upcoming deadlines. Off by default.
enabled.synonyms: enable, turn on, activate, switch on, reminders, deadline reminders, due-date reminders, advance notice, heads up, nudge before due

direction.label: Scan which side of now?
direction.description: 'future' (default) matches records whose dateField is still ahead, up to offsetHours out — upcoming-deadline reminders. 'past' matches records whose dateField is at least offsetHours behind now — act-after-the-fact policies. The emitted event and the dedup marker are identical either way.

targetEntity.synonyms: entity to monitor, entity to watch, record type, object type

template.synonyms: message text, reminder body, notification copy, alert message, what to say

dateField.label: Which date field is the deadline?

program.name: std-notification-center
program.description: std-notification-center — per-user notification preferences, web-push subscriptions, and the digest drain for suppressed notifications. Owns the two owner-scoped stores std-notify-on-event consults at dispatch time: NotificationPreference rows (per event key: mode instant/digest/off, channel override, per-user quiet hours) and PushSubscription rows (captured via the browser/push-subscribe flow — the shared service worker + PushManager subscription, persisted as flat endpoint/p256dh/auth credentials). The DigestDrain trait is the delivery half of every suppression std-notify-on-event records: an hourly cron tick scans NotificationRecord audit rows left undispatched for digest/quiet-hours reasons and at least `minAgeHours` old, delivers each by email (the digest channel), and marks it dispatched — the reminder-scheduler self-driving scan loop verbatim. Compose alongside std-notify-on-event: the listener suppresses and records, this atom captures subscriptions, edits preferences, and drains.

fields.name: personId
fields.description: Owner of this preference row — rows are meant to be private to their owner. Access predicates need an [identity] roster, so the binding organism (which declares one) owns the @read/@update scoping; the generic atom cannot.

fields.name: eventKey
fields.description: Event key this preference applies to (matches a listener's eventKey); blank = all events.

fields.name: channel
fields.description: Channel override for this user.

fields.name: mode
fields.description: Delivery mode: instant (default), digest (deferred to the drain cycle), or off (muted).
fields.synonyms: delivery mode, frequency, cadence, mute, defer

fields.name: quietHours
fields.description: Per-user quiet-hours window as "HH:MM-HH:MM" (e.g. 22:00-07:00); blank = disabled.
fields.synonyms: do not disturb, quiet window, night mode

fields.name: userId
fields.description: Owner of this browser push subscription. Owner-scoped access predicates belong to the binding organism's [identity] roster, as with NotificationPreference.

fields.name: endpoint

fields.name: p256dh

fields.name: auth

fields.name: createdAt

fields.name: lastError
